source: AUTHORED — ProbeAI interview content, not ABTalks cohort curriculum. Curriculum facts live in curriculum.json; these are our questions about it.

schema.assumes: built = they passed the mission and did the work | studied = they attempted it and failed | none = safe when they skipped it or never saw it
schema.looks_for: what a strong answer contains; read by the Evaluator and Feedback agents
schema.followup: single probe to use when the first answer stays surface-level

questions.question: You set up a virtual environment early on. In your own words, what problem does that actually solve?
questions.followup: Have you ever had two projects need different versions of the same package? What happened?
questions.looks_for: isolation between projects; version conflicts; reproducibility for anyone else cloning it

questions.question: You ran a model locally with Ollama. What is genuinely different about that versus calling a hosted API?
questions.followup: When would you actually choose the local one?
questions.looks_for: no per-token cost, data stays local, works offline; bounded by your own hardware, smaller models, slower

questions.question: Beyond being a backup, what does putting a project on GitHub give you?
questions.followup: What does a commit history let you do that a folder of files does not?
questions.looks_for: history and rollback, branching, collaboration, a deploy source for hosting platforms

questions.question: If you had to run an AI coding assistant with no internet at all, what would need to be in place?
questions.followup: What would you give up compared to a cloud assistant?
questions.looks_for: a local runtime like Ollama, a downloaded model, an editor extension pointed at localhost; weaker model quality

questions.question: Walk me through how you set your project environment up — and what went into version control versus what deliberately stayed out.
questions.followup: What is in your .gitignore, and why those entries specifically?
questions.looks_for: venv create/activate, pinned requirements.txt, .venv and .env excluded, secrets never committed

questions.question: How did you actually wire your editor to the local model — what was talking to what?
questions.followup: What did you have to configure to make the extension find Ollama?
questions.looks_for: Ollama serving on a local port, extension pointed at that base URL, model name matching a pulled model

questions.question: You put a React frontend in front of your first AI project. How did the frontend and the Python side actually talk, and what broke first?
questions.followup: How did you handle the wait while the model was generating?
questions.looks_for: HTTP calls to a local API, CORS or port issues, loading state, error handling on a slow call

questions.question: Someone clones your repo and it will not run. How do you debug that?
questions.followup: What is the most common cause in your experience?
questions.looks_for: check Python version, fresh venv, install requirements, missing .env keys, absolute paths baked in

questions.question: You have a Python backend and a React frontend in one repository. How would you structure that so the two can be deployed independently?
questions.followup: What has to be configurable rather than hardcoded for that to work?
questions.looks_for: separate build pipelines, API base URL as env config, CORS allowlist, no build-time coupling

questions.question: When would you put a self-hosted model into production instead of a hosted API? What drives that decision?
questions.followup: At what point does the maths flip?
questions.looks_for: data residency and privacy, per-token cost at volume, latency control, vendor lock-in; against GPU cost and ops burden

questions.question: A ten-person team keeps breaking builds because everyone's environment has drifted. What would you change?
questions.followup: How do you stop it from drifting again six months later?
questions.looks_for: lockfiles, containerised dev environment, CI running the same image, a reproducible bootstrap script

questions.question: How would you handle secrets across local development, CI, and production?
questions.followup: What happens the day a key leaks into a commit?
questions.looks_for: .env locally and gitignored, platform secret store in prod, CI secrets, rotation, never in the repo

questions.question: You worked with structured data early on. What makes data structured, and why does that make it easier to work with?
questions.followup: What is the first thing you check when you open a new CSV?
questions.looks_for: predictable schema, typed columns, queryable; checking nulls, dtypes, row counts, encoding

questions.question: Unstructured data was a separate day. What makes a PDF or a webpage harder to handle than a spreadsheet?
questions.followup: What did you have to do to a document before it was usable?
questions.looks_for: no schema, layout noise, inconsistent formatting; extraction and cleaning before anything else

questions.question: What is a knowledge base in the context of an AI application, and why build one at all?
questions.followup: Why not just put everything in the prompt?
questions.looks_for: curated retrievable source of truth; context windows are finite and expensive; grounding reduces hallucination

questions.question: If you were handed a thousand mixed PDFs and Word documents to make searchable, what would worry you first?
questions.followup: How would you know your extraction was any good?
questions.looks_for: extraction quality, scanned images needing OCR, tables, inconsistent structure, spot-checking output

questions.question: Walk me through your pipeline for turning a raw document into something usable. What were the actual stages?
questions.followup: Which stage produced the worst output, and how did you find out?
questions.looks_for: load, extract text, clean, chunk, attach metadata; inspecting intermediate output rather than trusting it

questions.question: How did you decide how to split your documents into chunks?
questions.followup: What went wrong with your first chunk size?
questions.looks_for: size and overlap chosen deliberately, splitting on structure not arbitrary characters, context lost at boundaries

questions.question: How did you handle messy rows — missing values, wrong types, duplicates?
questions.followup: Did you drop them or repair them, and how did you decide?
questions.looks_for: explicit strategy per column, dropping versus imputing as a judgement call, logging what was discarded

questions.question: What metadata would you attach to each chunk, and what would you use it for later?
questions.followup: How does that change what your retrieval can do?
questions.looks_for: source document, page or section, date, category; enables filtered retrieval and citations back to the source

questions.question: Your knowledge base has to stay current as source documents change. How would you design that?
questions.followup: Full rebuild or incremental update — how would you choose?
questions.looks_for: content hashing to detect change, incremental upsert, versioning, cost and staleness trade-off

questions.question: Ingestion of a large corpus is slow and keeps failing partway. How would you make that pipeline production-grade?
questions.followup: How do you avoid reprocessing everything after a failure?
questions.looks_for: batching, checkpointing, idempotent writes, retries with backoff, a dead-letter path for bad documents

questions.question: How would you design a system where structured records and unstructured documents both need to answer one question?
questions.followup: Where does the join actually happen?
questions.looks_for: shared identifiers, hybrid query across a database and a vector store, merging results before generation

questions.question: Your knowledge base contains documents different users are not all allowed to see. How do you handle that?
questions.followup: Why is filtering after retrieval risky?
questions.looks_for: permissions as chunk metadata, filter at query time not post-hoc, per-tenant isolation, audit trail

questions.question: Explain what an embedding is to someone who has never heard the term.
questions.followup: What does it mean for two embeddings to be close together?
questions.looks_for: text as a vector of numbers, position encodes meaning, nearby vectors mean similar meaning not similar spelling

questions.question: Why do you need a vector database at all — why not just store the vectors in a normal table?
questions.followup: What does it do that a SQL WHERE clause cannot?
questions.looks_for: similarity search rather than exact match, approximate nearest neighbour indexing, scale of comparisons

questions.question: When someone types a question, how does the system find the right documents?
questions.followup: Why does that work even when the wording is completely different?
questions.looks_for: query is embedded the same way, nearest vectors returned, semantic not keyword matching

questions.question: Two sentences use completely different words but mean the same thing. How could a computer tell?
questions.followup: Where would that approach fall down?
questions.looks_for: meaning mapped into a shared space; struggles with negation, jargon, and domain terms unseen in training

questions.question: Walk me through populating your vector database — from raw text to a stored, searchable record.
questions.followup: What did you store alongside the vector itself?
questions.looks_for: chunk, embed in batches, upsert with ids and metadata, keep the original text for display

questions.question: How did you pick your top-k, and what happened when you changed it?
questions.followup: What does too high actually cost you?
questions.looks_for: tested values against real queries; too low misses context, too high adds noise and tokens and dilutes the answer

questions.question: Which embedding model did you use, and what would break if you swapped it for a different one tomorrow?
questions.followup: Could you mix vectors from two models in one collection?
questions.looks_for: dimensions differ, vector spaces are not comparable, the whole collection must be re-embedded

questions.question: Your retrieval returns confidently wrong documents. How do you debug it?
questions.followup: Where in the pipeline would you look first?
questions.looks_for: inspect what was actually retrieved and its scores, check chunking, check the query embedding, test with known-good queries

questions.question: You are choosing a vector store for a production system. What drives that decision?
questions.followup: When would an in-process store stop being enough?
questions.looks_for: scale, persistence, filtering support, hosting and ops cost, latency; in-process breaks with multiple workers or restarts

questions.question: Pure semantic search misses exact matches like product codes or error numbers. How would you fix that?
questions.followup: How do you combine two sets of results that score on different scales?
questions.looks_for: hybrid search with keyword plus vector, reranking, score normalisation or reciprocal rank fusion

questions.question: Your corpus grows from ten thousand to fifty million vectors. What breaks first?
questions.followup: What would you trade to keep query latency acceptable?
questions.looks_for: index build time and memory, exact search infeasible, ANN with recall traded for speed, sharding, re-embedding cost

questions.question: Your embedding model is deprecated and you must migrate. How do you do that without downtime?
questions.followup: How would you know the new model is actually better?
questions.looks_for: re-embed into a parallel collection, dual-read or shadow traffic, cutover after evaluation on a fixed query set

questions.question: Explain RAG end to end, as if to a product manager.
questions.followup: Which part of that is the retrieval and which is the generation?
questions.looks_for: question in, retrieve relevant context, put it in the prompt, model answers from it, grounded and citable

questions.question: What is the difference between zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting?
questions.followup: Which one did you actually reach for most, and why?
questions.looks_for: no examples, examples in the prompt, asking for reasoning steps; each suited to different task shapes

questions.question: When would you fine-tune a model instead of just writing a better prompt?
questions.followup: Name one concrete signal that prompting has run out of road.
questions.looks_for: consistent format or style, narrow domain, latency and cost at volume; not for adding fresh facts

questions.question: A model keeps answering in the wrong format no matter how you ask. What would you try?
questions.followup: How would you know the change actually helped rather than got lucky once?
questions.looks_for: explicit format instruction, worked examples, structured output mode, testing on a fixed question set

questions.question: Walk me through your RAG pipeline as you built it — what happens between the user pressing enter and seeing an answer?
questions.followup: What was the slowest part, and did you measure it or guess?
questions.looks_for: embed query, retrieve, assemble prompt, call model, return; naming a measured bottleneck rather than a hunch

questions.question: You worked with function calling and structured outputs. How did you actually get reliable JSON back?
questions.followup: What did you do when the model returned something unparseable anyway?
questions.looks_for: schema passed to the API, JSON mode, validation on parse, retry or repair rather than trusting the output

questions.question: You did a hands-on fine-tune with LoRA. What did you actually change about the model?
questions.followup: Why is that cheaper than full fine-tuning?
questions.looks_for: small adapter matrices trained, base weights frozen, far fewer trainable parameters, fits on modest hardware

questions.question: How did you compare two versions of a system prompt and decide which was better?
questions.followup: What stopped that from being just your opinion?
questions.looks_for: fixed question set, consistent criteria, side-by-side comparison, recording results instead of impressions

questions.question: Your RAG system answers confidently from documents that do not support the answer. How do you engineer that out?
questions.followup: What would you have the model do when retrieval genuinely finds nothing?
questions.looks_for: instruct answering only from context, require citations, relevance thresholds, an explicit I-don't-know path

questions.question: Give me the decision criteria for prompting versus RAG versus fine-tuning. Real thresholds, not 'it depends'.
questions.followup: Which of those handles knowledge that changes weekly?
questions.looks_for: named criteria — data volatility, dataset size, latency budget, cost per request; RAG for changing facts, fine-tuning for form

questions.question: You are exposing tools to a model that can write to a production database. How do you design that safely?
questions.followup: What do you never let the model decide on its own?
questions.looks_for: narrow tool scope, validation server-side, confirmation for destructive actions, least privilege, audit logging

questions.question: You fine-tuned a model and it is worse on everything except your task. What happened, and what would you do?
questions.followup: How would you have caught that before shipping?
questions.looks_for: catastrophic forgetting or overfitting to a narrow set, holdout evaluation on general tasks, adapters kept separable

questions.question: You built a chatbot backend. What is the backend actually responsible for that the frontend cannot do?
questions.followup: Why can the API key not just live in the frontend?
questions.looks_for: holds secrets, calls the model, manages state and validation; anything in the browser is public

questions.question: Why does a chatbot need conversation memory at all — what breaks without it?
questions.followup: Where does that memory actually live between two requests?
questions.looks_for: models are stateless per call, follow-ups lose their referent; history resent each turn or stored server-side

questions.question: What does streaming a response change for the person using the chatbot?
questions.followup: Does it make the answer arrive any faster?
questions.looks_for: tokens appear immediately, perceived latency drops, total time is unchanged; the wait becomes tolerable

questions.question: What would make a chat interface feel broken to you, even when the answers are correct?
questions.followup: Which of those would you fix first?
questions.looks_for: no loading feedback, lost input, no error message, scroll jumping, no way to retry

questions.question: Walk me through your chat endpoint — what comes in, what goes out, and what happens in between?
questions.followup: How did you keep one user's conversation separate from another's?
questions.looks_for: request schema, session identifier, history assembly, model call, response shape; keyed state

questions.question: How did you get streamed tokens all the way from the model to the browser?
questions.followup: What broke the first time you tried it?
questions.looks_for: SSE or chunked response, async generator, frontend reading a stream incrementally; buffering or CORS problems

questions.question: Your conversation grows past what fits in the context window. What did you do about it?
questions.followup: What information did you lose, and did it matter?
questions.looks_for: truncation, sliding window, or summarising older turns; a conscious decision about what is discarded

questions.question: The model returns markdown, code blocks, and tables. How did you render that without it looking a mess?
questions.followup: What is the risk in rendering model output directly as HTML?
questions.looks_for: a markdown renderer, syntax highlighting, sanitisation; injection risk from unsanitised output

questions.question: Your chat state lives in server memory and you now need to run more than one instance. What breaks and how do you fix it?
questions.followup: What are you trading by moving that state out of the process?
questions.looks_for: requests hit different workers and lose state; move to shared store; added latency and a new dependency

questions.question: A user closes the tab mid-stream. What should happen server-side, and why does it matter?
questions.followup: What is still costing you money at that moment?
questions.looks_for: detect disconnect and cancel, stop token generation, persist partial state; tokens bill until cancelled

questions.question: Your chatbot needs to serve ten thousand concurrent users. Where do you expect it to fall over?
questions.followup: Which of those can you fix without touching the model?
questions.looks_for: provider rate limits, connection exhaustion, memory per session, cost; queueing, caching, autoscaling

questions.question: How would you design the frontend so a slow or failed model call never leaves the user stuck?
questions.followup: What does the user see at second thirty?
questions.looks_for: timeouts, retry affordance, streaming feedback, disabled resubmit, an explicit error state rather than a spinner forever

questions.question: What makes something an agent rather than just a model call in a loop?
questions.followup: What is the model actually deciding?
questions.looks_for: chooses actions and tools, observes results, iterates toward a goal; control flow driven by the model

questions.question: What problem does MCP solve? Why does it exist?
questions.followup: What was clumsy before it?
questions.looks_for: a standard protocol between models and tools or data; bespoke per-app integrations replaced by reusable servers

questions.question: Why would you use several specialised agents instead of one agent that does everything?
questions.followup: What does that cost you?
questions.looks_for: focused prompts, independently testable, easier to change; more calls, more latency, coordination overhead

questions.question: If you gave a model the ability to run actions on your behalf, what would you be nervous about?
questions.followup: How would you sleep at night shipping that?
questions.looks_for: wrong or irreversible actions, loops, cost, prompt injection; scoping, confirmation, limits, logging

questions.question: Walk me through a tool you gave an agent — the definition, and how the model knew when to call it.
questions.followup: What happened when it called the tool with bad arguments?
questions.looks_for: name, description, typed parameters; the description drives selection; server-side validation and error feedback

questions.question: How did your agents pass work between each other?
questions.followup: Did one call the next directly, or did something coordinate them?
questions.looks_for: shared state or an orchestrator, defined handoff contract, avoiding direct coupling between agents

questions.question: You built or connected an MCP server. What did it expose, and how did the client discover it?
questions.followup: What is the difference between a tool and a resource there?
questions.looks_for: tools and resources declared, client lists capabilities on connect; tools act, resources supply data

questions.question: Your agent gets stuck calling the same tool over and over. How do you stop that?
questions.followup: How do you make it fail usefully rather than silently?
questions.looks_for: iteration cap, loop detection, tool results fed back clearly, terminal error surfaced to the user

questions.question: How would you design a multi-agent system so one agent's failure does not take down the whole interaction?
questions.followup: Which agent would you make degradable, and to what?
questions.looks_for: isolated failures, timeouts per agent, deterministic fallbacks, partial results still useful

questions.question: An MCP server exposes tools to any connecting client. What are the security implications?
questions.followup: How do you scope what a given client can reach?
questions.looks_for: authentication, per-client permissions, least privilege on tools, no ambient credentials, audit logging

questions.question: Agentic systems are non-deterministic. How do you test one?
questions.followup: What would you assert on, if not the exact output?
questions.looks_for: mocked tools, asserting tool-call sequences and invariants, evaluation sets with scoring, snapshot review

questions.question: A tool returns text from an untrusted source and the model starts following instructions inside it. What is happening, and how do you defend?
questions.followup: Why is telling the model to ignore such instructions not enough?
questions.looks_for: indirect prompt injection; treat tool output as data, isolate untrusted content, constrain privileges, never rely on prompt-level pleading

questions.question: How do you tell whether a chatbot is actually any good?
questions.followup: What would you measure, given the answers are free text?
questions.looks_for: a fixed evaluation set, criteria like accuracy and groundedness, human review, regression checks over versions

questions.question: What is a guardrail in an AI application, and where does it sit?
questions.followup: Input side, output side, or both?
questions.looks_for: checks around the model, not inside it; input filtering and output validation both needed

questions.question: What does putting your app in a container actually get you?
questions.followup: What does 'it works on my machine' mean once you have one?
questions.looks_for: environment shipped with the code, reproducible across machines, same image in CI and production

questions.question: Your AI feature works well but the monthly bill is far too high. Where would you look first?
questions.followup: What is the cheapest change that usually helps most?
questions.looks_for: token volume per request, oversized context, model tier, call frequency; caching and trimming context

questions.question: How did you test your chatbot? Walk me through what you actually ran.
questions.followup: What did you assert, given the output changes every time?
questions.looks_for: fixed inputs, mocked model for deterministic paths, checks on structure and required content rather than exact strings

questions.question: What did you do specifically to reduce cost or latency, and how much did it move?
questions.followup: Did you measure before and after, or estimate?
questions.looks_for: a named change — smaller model, trimmed context, caching, fewer calls — with an actual measured delta

questions.question: How did you stop your app leaking secrets or personal data into a model prompt?
questions.followup: What is in your prompt right now that should not be?
questions.looks_for: keys server-side only, redaction of PII before sending, awareness of what history carries, provider retention policy

questions.question: Walk me through your Dockerfile. What is in each stage and why?
questions.followup: What made the image smaller?
questions.looks_for: base image choice, dependency layer cached before source, multi-stage build, no secrets baked in

questions.question: How would you catch a quality regression before your users do, when a prompt change can silently degrade answers?
questions.followup: What runs in CI, and what has to be human?
questions.looks_for: evaluation suite gating deploys, scored against a golden set, drift alerts; humans for nuance and edge cases

questions.question: Design the guardrails for an AI assistant that handles customer data. What layers do you put in?
questions.followup: Which layer do you trust least?
questions.looks_for: input validation, PII redaction, output filtering, rate limits, human escalation; prompt-level rules are the weakest

questions.question: When is Kubernetes the wrong answer for deploying an AI service?
questions.followup: What would you run instead, and at what point would you change your mind?
questions.looks_for: operational cost outweighs benefit at small scale; managed container hosting until scale, multi-service or GPU scheduling justify it

questions.question: Your model provider has an outage in the middle of the day. What does your system do?
questions.followup: What is the honest cost of that fallback?
questions.looks_for: timeouts and retries with backoff, circuit breaker, fallback model or cached path, degrading honestly rather than hanging

questions.question: What would you want to see on a dashboard for a live AI application?
questions.followup: Which single number tells you something is wrong right now?
questions.looks_for: error rate, latency, request volume, token cost; one leading indicator rather than a wall of charts

questions.question: What does 'production ready' mean to you, concretely?
questions.followup: What is the last thing you check before shipping?
questions.looks_for: handles failure, observable, configurable per environment, tested, deployable and reversible

questions.question: Tell me what you built for your capstone and what it actually does.
questions.followup: Which part are you proudest of, and which part is held together with tape?
questions.looks_for: a clear description of the system, honest ownership of both the strong and the fragile parts

questions.question: Something is wrong in production but no user has complained yet. How would you find out?
questions.followup: What has to be in place beforehand for that to work?
questions.looks_for: monitoring and alerting on real signals, health checks, logs you can search, thresholds set in advance

questions.question: What do you log on each request, and what would you refuse to log?
questions.followup: Could you trace one user's failing request through your logs right now?
questions.looks_for: request id, timing, outcome, model and token counts; never secrets or raw personal data; correlation across steps

questions.question: How did you handle configuration differences between local development and deployment?
questions.followup: What broke the first time you deployed?
questions.looks_for: environment variables, no hardcoded URLs or keys, CORS and port differences, sensible defaults

questions.question: Take the hardest bug you hit in your capstone. What was it, and how did you find it?
questions.followup: What did you change so it could not happen again?
questions.looks_for: a specific, real bug with a debugging method rather than guesswork, and a structural fix or test afterwards

questions.question: How would you verify a deployment actually worked, beyond the page loading?
questions.followup: What would you automate?
questions.looks_for: health endpoint, smoke test of the real path, checking logs and error rate after release, rollback ready

questions.question: How would you design observability for a system where the failure is a bad answer rather than an exception?
questions.followup: What signal tells you quality dropped when nothing crashed?
questions.looks_for: logging inputs and outputs for sampling, user feedback capture, offline scoring, tracking refusal and fallback rates

questions.question: If you rebuilt your capstone from scratch with everything you know now, what would you do differently and why?
questions.followup: What would you keep exactly as it is?
questions.looks_for: specific architectural regrets with reasoning, not a wish list; ability to defend what worked

questions.question: Take the full pipeline — ingestion, retrieval, generation, agents, deployment. Under real load, what breaks first?
questions.followup: How would you harden that one thing without rewriting everything?
questions.looks_for: names a specific weakest link with reasoning about why, and a targeted incremental fix

questions.question: You are handing this system to another engineer tomorrow and going on leave. What have you not done that you should have?
questions.followup: What would they get wrong first?
questions.looks_for: honest gaps — documentation, tests, runbooks, unclear ownership of config and secrets; awareness of implicit knowledge

questions.question: What does requirements.txt give you that just installing packages as you need them does not?
questions.followup: What happens six months later on a different machine?
questions.looks_for: pinned versions, reproducible install, anyone can recreate the environment from the file

questions.question: You downloaded a model to run locally. What decides whether your machine can actually run it?
questions.followup: What happens if it does not fit?
questions.looks_for: parameter count and quantisation versus available RAM or VRAM; spills to disk or CPU and becomes unusably slow

questions.question: What is an API key really, and why does it need protecting?
questions.followup: Where should it live once the app is deployed?
questions.looks_for: identifies and bills you, acts as a password; server-side environment variable, never in frontend code or the repo

questions.question: You want to show your project to someone who has no Python installed. What are your options?
questions.followup: Which would you pick, and what does it cost you?
questions.looks_for: deploy it somewhere public, containerise, or record a demo; hosting is the real answer and needs config for it

questions.question: How do you decide what belongs in requirements.txt versus what was just an experiment?
questions.followup: How would you check nothing unused is in there?
questions.looks_for: direct dependencies only rather than raw pip freeze; verify by installing into a clean environment and running

questions.question: Your local model runs but is unusably slow. What do you check?
questions.followup: What would you change first?
questions.looks_for: model size against RAM, CPU versus GPU, quantised variant, context length, other processes competing

questions.question: How did you run the React dev server and the Python server at the same time during development?
questions.followup: What did CORS have to do with it?
questions.looks_for: two ports, a dev proxy or CORS middleware, API base URL as configuration rather than hardcoded

questions.question: Your editor flags an import as unresolved but the code runs fine. What is going on?
questions.followup: How do you fix it properly rather than ignoring the squiggle?
questions.looks_for: editor pointed at a different interpreter than the venv; select the correct interpreter, not suppress the warning

questions.question: How would you make your project set up in a single command on a brand new machine?
questions.followup: What is still manual, and could it be automated?
questions.looks_for: bootstrap script or task runner, containerised dev environment, documented prerequisites, no hidden manual steps

questions.question: Your company forbids sending any data to external AI APIs. Design the coding-assistant setup.
questions.followup: What quality do you give up?
questions.looks_for: self-hosted models on internal hardware, a shared inference server, editor pointed internally; smaller models perform worse

questions.question: How would you set up CI for a repo holding both a Python backend and a React frontend?
questions.followup: What runs on every commit versus only on release?
questions.looks_for: separate jobs per stack, dependency caching, lint and test on every push, build and deploy gated on the main branch

questions.question: How would you decide which local model a whole team should standardise on?
questions.followup: How would you compare them fairly?
questions.looks_for: benchmark on the team's real tasks, lowest common hardware, licence terms, quantisation support; a fixed comparison set

questions.question: What is a schema, and how does having one help you?
questions.followup: What do you do when the source keeps changing it?
questions.looks_for: an agreed shape and types, lets you validate early; versioning and validation at the boundary when it drifts

questions.question: Why can you not just load a very large CSV straight into memory?
questions.followup: What would you do instead?
questions.looks_for: the file exceeds available RAM; read in chunks, stream, or use a columnar format and process incrementally

questions.question: What is OCR, and when do you have no choice but to use it?
questions.followup: Why is it a source of errors?
questions.looks_for: scanned pages are images with no text layer; recognition quality varies with scan quality, columns and tables

questions.question: Two documents in your knowledge base contradict each other. What should the system do?
questions.followup: How would it even know they conflict?
questions.looks_for: surface both with sources rather than silently choosing; recency or authority metadata to break the tie

questions.question: How did you validate structured data before it entered your pipeline?
questions.followup: What happened to the rows that failed?
questions.looks_for: schema validation and type coercion at the boundary; failures quarantined and logged rather than silently dropped

questions.question: A PDF has two columns and a table. What actually happens when you extract it naively?
questions.followup: How did you deal with that?
questions.looks_for: reading order scrambles across columns, tables flatten into nonsense; a layout-aware parser or per-format handling

questions.question: How would you process a data file far larger than your machine's memory?
questions.followup: How would you test that code without a huge file?
questions.looks_for: chunked iteration and generators, aggregate incrementally, never materialise everything; test on a small fixture

questions.question: How did you stop the same document being added to your knowledge base twice?
questions.followup: What counts as 'the same document' when the file was edited?
questions.looks_for: stable deterministic ids or content hashing, upsert rather than insert; changed content means replace not duplicate

questions.question: Design an ingestion pipeline handling ten file formats without turning into a wall of if-statements.
questions.followup: Where does format-specific logic actually live?
questions.looks_for: a parser per format behind one interface, registry or strategy pattern, all producing the same normalised output

questions.question: Source data quality is poor and the upstream team will not fix it. How do you protect your system?
questions.followup: What do you show users about it?
questions.looks_for: validate at the boundary, quarantine bad records, track quality metrics, be honest about coverage gaps

questions.question: Users need to trace an answer back to the exact source document and page. What does that require?
questions.followup: What has to be captured at ingestion time for that to be possible?
questions.looks_for: provenance metadata per chunk — document id, page, offsets — carried through retrieval and surfaced as a citation

questions.question: A document must be deleted for legal reasons. Walk me through everything that has to happen.
questions.followup: What is easy to miss?
questions.looks_for: source file, derived chunks, vectors, caches and backups; deletion has to propagate everywhere it was copied

questions.question: What is a collection in a vector database?
questions.followup: Why not put everything into one big collection?
questions.looks_for: a group of vectors sharing an embedding space and schema; separation by domain, permissions or model

questions.question: What does 'nearest neighbour' mean here, and what makes it approximate?
questions.followup: What are you giving up by accepting approximate?
questions.looks_for: closest vectors by a distance measure; ANN skips exhaustive comparison, trading a little recall for large speed gains

questions.question: Why embed documents in batches rather than one at a time?
questions.followup: What limits how big a batch can be?
questions.looks_for: far fewer round trips and much better throughput; bounded by memory and provider request limits

questions.question: Does an embedding actually understand the text, or is it doing something else?
questions.followup: Why does that distinction matter in practice?
questions.looks_for: statistical patterns from training, not comprehension; explains failures on negation, novel jargon and domain terms

questions.question: What id scheme did you use for your vectors, and why does that choice matter?
questions.followup: What happens when you re-ingest the same document?
questions.looks_for: deterministic ids derived from source plus chunk index, so re-ingestion upserts over the old vectors instead of duplicating

questions.question: How did you combine metadata filtering with similarity search?
questions.followup: Does the filter apply before or after the search, and why does that matter?
questions.looks_for: a where clause on metadata; pre-filtering shrinks the candidate set and changes what top-k can return

questions.question: Your embedding job dies halfway through fifty thousand documents. What now?
questions.followup: How would you make it resumable next time?
questions.looks_for: checkpoint progress, idempotent upserts keyed by id so re-running is safe, track completed batches

questions.question: How did you actually inspect what your retrieval was returning?
questions.followup: What surprised you when you looked?
questions.looks_for: printing retrieved chunks with similarity scores, checking against a known query set rather than trusting the output

questions.question: You must re-embed the entire corpus with zero downtime. Design it.
questions.followup: How does the switchover actually happen?
questions.looks_for: build a parallel collection in the background, dual-read or alias, cut over after validation, keep rollback available

questions.question: One collection per customer, or one shared collection with a tenant field?
questions.followup: What breaks at a thousand customers?
questions.looks_for: isolation and easy deletion versus per-collection overhead; thousands of collections strain the store, shared needs strict filtering

questions.question: Users say search 'feels worse' but you changed nothing. What could have happened?
questions.followup: How would you prove it either way?
questions.looks_for: corpus grew or drifted, query mix changed, index rebuilt; a fixed evaluation set measured over time settles it

questions.question: Chunk size, overlap and top-k all interact. How would you tune them together?
questions.followup: What do you measure to know you improved?
questions.looks_for: they jointly control recall and prompt size; sweep against a fixed query set with a scored metric rather than by feel

questions.question: What is the context window, and how does it constrain a RAG system?
questions.followup: What do you cut when it is full?
questions.looks_for: a hard token budget covering prompt and response; drop least-relevant chunks, trim history, keep the question intact

questions.question: What is a structured output, and why is it worth the effort?
questions.followup: What is the alternative, and why is it worse?
questions.looks_for: schema-constrained JSON the code can rely on; parsing free-form prose is brittle and breaks silently

questions.question: What data do you actually need before you can fine-tune anything?
questions.followup: How much is enough?
questions.looks_for: input-output pairs in the exact target format; quality and consistency matter more than raw volume

questions.question: What does quantisation mean, and why would you use it?
questions.followup: What is the trade-off?
questions.looks_for: storing weights at lower precision, cutting memory and speeding inference, at some cost to output quality

questions.question: Show me how your system prompt was structured — what was in it, and in what order?
questions.followup: What did you take out because it was not helping?
questions.looks_for: role, constraints, context, output format as distinct sections; evidence of iterating by removal, not just addition

questions.question: How did you define a tool for the model — what did the description have to contain?
questions.followup: What happened when two tools did similar things?
questions.looks_for: the description is what drives selection; typed parameters; overlapping tools cause wrong or oscillating choices

questions.question: What did you set for your LoRA run, and what did each setting actually do?
questions.followup: Which would you change first if it underfit?
questions.looks_for: rank, alpha, learning rate, epochs and what they control; rank and learning rate as the first levers to move

questions.question: Your RAG answer is correct but takes fifteen seconds. Where did the time go?
questions.followup: What could run in parallel?
questions.looks_for: measure embedding, retrieval and generation separately; generation usually dominates; retrieval work can overlap

questions.question: Prompts behave like code but rarely get reviewed like code. How would you version and review them?
questions.followup: What does a prompt change request look like?
questions.looks_for: prompts in version control, diffed and reviewed, an evaluation run attached to the change, rollback possible

questions.question: Your fine-tuned model needs updating every month as the domain shifts. Is fine-tuning still right?
questions.followup: What would you move to?
questions.looks_for: retraining cost compounds; retrieve volatile facts and fine-tune only for stable form and style

questions.question: How would you design a tool-calling system where the model can never fabricate a tool result?
questions.followup: How would you detect it if it tried?
questions.looks_for: results enter context only from real execution, never model-authored; validate returned ids and values against the source

questions.question: Your team wants to fine-tune because 'the prompt has got too long'. How do you respond?
questions.followup: What would you measure to settle the argument?
questions.looks_for: challenges the premise; compares trimming context and retrieval against tuning cost, measured on accuracy and cost per request

questions.question: What state does a chat interface have to keep track of?
questions.followup: What goes wrong if you get it wrong?
questions.looks_for: message list, in-flight request, input draft, error state; duplicate sends, lost typing, stuck spinners

questions.question: Why format model output at all, rather than printing the raw text?
questions.followup: What does the user actually gain?
questions.looks_for: readable structure, code blocks, lists and tables; faster scanning and comprehension

questions.question: The model returns a link or an image and you render it. What is the risk?
questions.followup: How would you handle that?
questions.looks_for: unsafe or phishing content and script injection; sanitise, restrict what can render, escape by default

questions.question: Where would you put rate limiting in a chat app, and what are you protecting?
questions.followup: What does a legitimate heavy user experience?
questions.looks_for: at the API boundary before the model call; protects cost, provider quota and availability; needs a clear limit message

questions.question: How did you handle the message list re-rendering while tokens streamed in?
questions.followup: Did you hit performance problems?
questions.looks_for: appending to the last message with stable keys, avoiding full list re-render, scroll anchoring at the bottom

questions.question: How did you render code blocks with syntax highlighting?
questions.followup: What was fiddly about adding a copy button?
questions.looks_for: markdown renderer plus a highlighter, language from the fence; clipboard API, copying source not rendered markup

questions.question: How did you decide what to keep in the conversation history and what to drop?
questions.followup: Did you ever summarise older turns, and what did that cost?
questions.looks_for: a token budget with a recency window; summarising costs an extra call and loses specific detail

questions.question: Streaming works locally but arrives all at once in production. What would you look at?
questions.followup: Why does a proxy matter here?
questions.looks_for: reverse proxy or CDN buffering the response, compression, missing streaming headers, chunked transfer disabled

questions.question: How would you version your chat API so an older frontend does not break?
questions.followup: When is it acceptable to break compatibility?
questions.looks_for: additive changes by default, versioned routes when breaking, a deprecation window with both live

questions.question: Design the chat experience for someone on a poor mobile connection.
questions.followup: What happens if the connection drops mid-answer?
questions.looks_for: preserved input, clear pending state, retry that does not duplicate, resumable or restartable request, no silent failure

questions.question: Users want to export a conversation as a formatted report. How would you design that?
questions.followup: Where should the formatting logic live?
questions.looks_for: render server-side from the stored structured messages, not by scraping the rendered DOM; one source of truth

questions.question: Streaming makes error handling harder. Why, and what do you do about it?
questions.followup: How do you report a failure after you have already sent a success status?
questions.looks_for: headers and status go out before the failure happens; in-stream error events, and a client that handles partial output

questions.question: What does an orchestrator do in a multi-agent system?
questions.followup: Why not just let the agents call each other directly?
questions.looks_for: routes work, sequences agents, owns shared state; direct calls create coupling, cycles and untestable agents

questions.question: What changed about your chatbot once you made it agentic?
questions.followup: What got harder?
questions.looks_for: it can take actions rather than only answer; latency, cost, non-determinism and debugging all get worse

questions.question: In MCP, who runs the server — the model, or your application?
questions.followup: What connects to what?
questions.looks_for: the server is a separate process exposing tools and resources; the host application connects as client and offers them to the model

questions.question: When should a chatbot deliberately not use an agent?
questions.followup: What does using one anyway cost you?
questions.looks_for: simple deterministic tasks with a known path; agents add latency, cost and unpredictability for no benefit

questions.question: How did your agent know it was finished?
questions.followup: What stopped it from running forever?
questions.looks_for: an explicit terminal condition or final-answer signal, plus a hard iteration cap as a backstop

questions.question: How did you debug a multi-agent run that produced the wrong result?
questions.followup: What did you have to log to make that possible?
questions.looks_for: each agent's inputs and outputs captured, step-by-step trace, ability to replay one agent in isolation

questions.question: How did you test your MCP server without wiring up a full client?
questions.followup: What did you assert on?
questions.looks_for: invoking tools directly, validating declared schemas, inspector tooling; asserting shape and error handling

questions.question: Your agentic chatbot is far slower than the plain one. Where did the time go?
questions.followup: What would you cut first?
questions.looks_for: several sequential model calls plus tool round trips; parallelise independent steps or skip agents when not needed

questions.question: How would you add a new agent to an existing pipeline without touching the others?
questions.followup: What contract makes that possible?
questions.looks_for: agents read and write shared state with a defined trigger and output, no direct references between them

questions.question: Why would you expose your product's capabilities over MCP at all?
questions.followup: What does that cost you?
questions.looks_for: one integration reusable by many clients instead of bespoke ones; ongoing maintenance, versioning and a wider security surface

questions.question: The model decides how many calls to make, so cost is unpredictable. How do you control that?
questions.followup: What is your hard stop?
questions.looks_for: per-session iteration and token budgets, per-user caps, monitoring on spend, failing closed rather than looping

questions.question: How do you decide what belongs in a tool versus what belongs in the prompt?
questions.followup: What is the sign you got that boundary wrong?
questions.looks_for: dynamic, large or side-effecting things become tools; stable rules stay in the prompt; bloated prompts or invented data are the symptoms

questions.question: What is a golden set, and why do you need one?
questions.followup: How do you keep it honest over time?
questions.looks_for: a fixed set of inputs with known-good expectations; refresh carefully or you end up tuning to the test

questions.question: Which costs you more — a long prompt or a long answer?
questions.followup: How does that change what you optimise first?
questions.looks_for: output tokens are typically priced higher than input; capping response length often beats trimming context

questions.question: Explain prompt injection in plain terms.
questions.followup: Who is the attacker in that scenario?
questions.looks_for: untrusted text carrying instructions the model obeys; either the end user or whoever authored a retrieved document

questions.question: What is the difference between an image and a container?
questions.followup: Which one holds your data?
questions.looks_for: the image is the built artifact, the container a running instance; containers are ephemeral, persistence needs volumes

questions.question: The model answers differently every run. How did you write tests against that?
questions.followup: Did setting temperature to zero solve it?
questions.looks_for: mock the model for unit tests, assert properties and structure rather than exact strings; zero temperature helps but guarantees nothing

questions.question: Where in your pipeline would caching genuinely help?
questions.followup: What is the risk of caching model responses?
questions.looks_for: embeddings and repeated identical queries cache well; stale answers and personalised content leaking between users

questions.question: How did you validate what a user sends before it ever reaches the model?
questions.followup: What did you reject outright?
questions.looks_for: length caps, type and schema validation, content checks; oversized or malformed input rejected at the boundary

questions.question: Your container runs locally but crashes on the hosting platform. How do you diagnose it?
questions.followup: What are the usual suspects?
questions.looks_for: read platform logs first; architecture mismatch, missing environment variables, wrong port binding, memory limits

questions.question: How would you use one model to grade another model's answers, and where would you not trust it?
questions.followup: How do you check the judge itself is any good?
questions.looks_for: rubric-based scoring to scale evaluation; biased toward length and its own style; calibrate against human-labelled examples

questions.question: You must halve AI spend without users noticing. What is your plan, in order?
questions.followup: What is the last resort?
questions.looks_for: measure where spend goes first, then cache, trim context, cap output, route easy queries to a cheaper model; quality cuts last

questions.question: Design defence in depth for an assistant exposed to the public internet.
questions.followup: Which layer do you assume will be bypassed?
questions.looks_for: layered input and output controls, least privilege on tools, rate limits, monitoring; assume prompt-level instructions fail

questions.question: How would you deploy a stateful chat service with no downtime?
questions.followup: What happens to conversations that are mid-flight?
questions.looks_for: rolling deploy behind health checks, drain connections before shutdown, state held outside the process so sessions survive

questions.question: What is the difference between logging and monitoring?
questions.followup: Which of the two wakes you up at night?
questions.looks_for: logs are the detailed record, monitoring aggregates signals and alerts on them; alerting is what pages you

questions.question: What is a health check actually for?
questions.followup: What should it deliberately not do?
questions.looks_for: lets the platform know the instance is alive and ready; must be fast and must not call paid external APIs

questions.question: If you had one more week on your capstone, what would you spend it on?
questions.followup: Why that ahead of everything else?
questions.looks_for: a prioritisation argument grounded in a real weakness of what they built, not a generic wish list

questions.question: What would you put in a runbook for whoever is on call at 3am?
questions.followup: What is the very first thing they should check?
questions.looks_for: symptoms mapped to actions, where the dashboards and logs are, how to roll back, who to escalate to

questions.question: How would you trace one request across several agents or services?
questions.followup: What has to be passed along for that to work?
questions.looks_for: a correlation id generated at the entry point, propagated through every call and logged at each step

questions.question: How did you handle required configuration — what happens if an environment variable is missing?
questions.followup: Fail at startup, or at first use?
questions.looks_for: validate required config at startup and fail fast with a clear message; optional values get sensible defaults

questions.question: How did you demo your capstone — what could have gone wrong live, and how did you prepare?
questions.followup: What was your fallback if it broke on stage?
questions.looks_for: rehearsed path, seeded data, minimal live dependencies, a recording or local fallback ready

questions.question: Your logs are enormous and mostly useless. How would you fix that?
questions.followup: What do you keep?
questions.looks_for: use levels properly, structured fields instead of prose, sample high-volume events, set retention; always keep errors and key transitions

questions.question: How would you roll a risky change out to ten percent of users first?
questions.followup: What signal decides whether you continue or roll back?
questions.looks_for: feature flag or canary with cohort routing, compare error rate and latency against the control, automated rollback

questions.question: What service level would you commit to for an AI feature, and why is that harder than for a normal API?
questions.followup: How would you measure the quality half of it?
questions.looks_for: latency and availability are measurable; answer quality needs proxies — user feedback, fallback rate, evaluation scores

questions.question: Someone says your capstone would never survive real users. Argue back with specifics.
questions.followup: Where would you concede the point?
questions.looks_for: a reasoned defence naming actual mitigations they built, and honest concession on the genuinely weak parts

questions.question: This system has to keep running for a year without you. What would you automate first?
questions.followup: What can never be automated away?
questions.looks_for: deploys, alerting, cleanup jobs, dependency updates; incident judgement and design decisions still need a person
